## Probability Die is loaded given the number rolled

(1) You walk into the “occasionally dishonest casino” with prior probabilities and likelihoods set to the values in slides 21-25 of lecture #5. (that is, a “loaded” die has a 10% chance of getting a 1-5 and a 50% chance of getting a 6 but 99% of the dice are fair)

![](images/clipboard-1559043268.png)

```{r casino}
## frequencies
frequency_fair = .99
frequency_loaded = .01

## for loaded die
p_6_given_loaded = .5 # P(six|D_loaded)
p_not_6_given_loaded = .5 # P(six_c|D_loaded)

## for an unloaded die
p_not_6_given_unloaded = 5/6 # P(six|D_unloaded)
p_6_given_unloaded = 1/6 # P(six_c|D_unloaded)


## probability 6 and loaded 
## P(6|L)*P(L) or P(L|6)*P(6)
P_6_and_loaded = p_6_given_loaded * frequency_loaded

## probability 6 and unloaded 
## P(6|UL)*P(UL) or P(UL|6)*P(6)
P_6_and_unloaded = p_6_given_unloaded * frequency_unloaded

```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
